title: HowlForge Checkpoint
description: The machine readable core of a handoff bundle. Every field exists because its absence would force the replacement worker to guess. The contract this serves: the next worker must be able to continue safely without the previous worker's session transcript.

task_id.description: Task identity, shared with HowlBoard and HowlPlane.

role.description: The workforce role the departing worker filled.

runtime.description: The client the work was performed through.

model.description: The model that performed the work.

worker.description: Richer worker identity when it is known.

session_id.description: Recorded for audit only. Nothing attempts to reattach to it: sessions are disposable.

runtime_identity.description: Richer runtime identity when it is known.

status.description: How far the departing worker got. An abandoned attempt must not be built on.

safe_to_resume.description: The departing worker's own verdict. It is believed: HowlForge never overrides a worker's caution.

last_verified_commit.description: The commit at which the recorded verification results were observed. Without it the resume rules have nothing to check.

dirty.description: Whether the working tree had uncommitted changes. A dirty tree the checkpoint does not record forces reconciliation.

remaining.description: Outstanding work. A partial checkpoint must list this explicitly.

changed_files.description: Repository relative paths. Absolute paths and parent traversal are refused.

decisions.description: Choices the replacement must not silently re-litigate.

unresolved_questions.description: Open questions. Their presence forces reconciliation rather than blocking, because an unanswered question is not a failure, it is a reason to look before continuing.
